title: 4ww-4-winds
label: "The Technical Spectacle" Jerms

won.source: The fed's own Maelstrom III: Legacy: "Winner and the new 4 Winds Champion, Jerms!!!"

how: Won the inaugural 4 Winds Championship tournament, beating Furiously Addictive Wrestling's own Apocalypse in the final. First ever 4 Winds Champion.
note: His own roster card bills him "1st Ever 4 Winds Wrestling Champion (Won the Tourney at M3: Legacy, Current Champ)"; nothing in the surviving record takes the belt off him.

title: 4ww-north-wind
label: Jay Phoenix

won.source: The fed's own first StormFront, recapped in the Tempest video package of 17 July 2003 (promotions/4ww/archive/tempest-2003-07-17.html); the awards site's own Hall of Fame ballot names him "First Ever NWT Champion".

how: Won a gauntlet, pinning Patti Anderson, Johnny Beckett, Nick Raynes and finally Jaime with the Firestorm. First ever North Wind Champion.
note: The show itself is not held — its row carries the collected edge — and the reign is receipted to the Tempest recap package, to Jay Phoenix's own Tempest interview ("How does it feel to be the FIRST champ?") and to the awards-site ballot.

title: 4ww-north-wind
label: "The Brute Force" Syxx Figures

won.source: The fed's own StormFront of 3 August 2003.

how: Pinned Jay Phoenix after Impulse passed him a coal miner's glove at ringside and he struck Phoenix in the face with it.

title: 4ww-north-wind
label: Jaime

won.source: The fed's own StormFront of 7 September 2003.

how: Beat Syxx Figures after Jay Phoenix, returning to the fed that night, took Syxx down; the show closes on Phoenix sitting in the ring watching Jaime leave with the belt.

title: 4ww-north-wind
label: "The Savior" Todd Dream

won.source: The fed's own Maelstrom I: Critical Mass.

how: Beat Jaime in the Maelstrom I main event after Sean Summers and Mike Marvelous interfered repeatedly; Jay Phoenix, booked into the title picture, was written out of the card in-fiction before the bell.
note: The awards site's own Hall of Fame ballot bills Todd Dream "Longest Ever NWT Reign".

title: 4ww-north-wind
label: "The Darling of the 4WW" Patti Anderson

won.source: The fed's own Maelstrom III: Legacy, dated March 2004 by its own closing copyright line.

how: Beat Todd Dream in the Maelstrom III main event with Jay Phoenix as special guest referee. Phoenix counted the fall; Dream and Jerms then attacked him, Jerms clubbing him in the back of the head with the 4 Winds trophy belt as the credits rolled.
note: Her own roster card bills her "North Wind Champion"; the awards ballot's own Best North Wind Champion of 2004 category lists Patti Anderson-McClancy, Kyo Kushinaga and Todd Dream, so the belt moved again later in 2004 in a sequence the surviving record does not fix.

title: 4ww-south-wind
label: "The Darling of the 4WW" Patti Anderson

won.source: The fed's own card preview for StormFront of 20 July 2003, whose main event is the ladder match that determined the title; her own roster card bills her "First Ever South Wind Champion".

how: Won the ladder match between the winners of the fed's own two South Wind mini tournaments. First ever South Wind Champion.
note: The 20 July card is not held — its row carries the collected edge — and the reign is receipted to the preview page and to her own roster card.

title: 4ww-south-wind
label: "Insane" Chris West

won.source: The recap package opening the fed's own StormFront of 7 September 2003: "West falling on Patti to make the pin... A new South Wind Champion."

how: Pinned Patti Anderson off a SkyTwister Press on the StormFront before 7 September 2003.
note: The show itself is not held; the date is the Sunday StormFront preceding the held 7 September card, at circa precision.

title: 4ww-south-wind
label: "Mr. Main Event" Mike Marvelous

won.source: The fed's own Maelstrom I: Critical Mass, where he defends and retains the belt twice.

note: How he took it from Chris West is not in the surviving record.

title: 4ww-south-wind
label: "The Technical Spectacle" Jerms

won.source: The fed's own Maelstrom II: Eruption, where he defends the belt against Jade.

how: Held the belt into Maelstrom II; his own roster card bills him a 4WW South Wind Champion.

title: 4ww-south-wind
label: Jade

won.source: The fed's own Maelstrom II: Eruption.

how: Beat Jerms at Maelstrom II. "The winner and NEW South Wind Champion...JADE!"

title: 4ww-south-wind
label: Bullet

won.source: The fed's own Maelstrom III: Legacy.

how: Beat 'Deathscythe Outlaw' Josh Starwind for the belt at Maelstrom III after winning a fatal four-way earlier the same night.

won.source: the fed's own Official 4WW Title History thread (promotions/4ww/archive/forum-official-4ww-title-history.html): "SF: 5/31/04- Chris Sanchez defeats Bullet to become the new South Wind Champion."

title: 4ww-south-wind
label: "The Modern Messiah" Darek DeAngelo

won.source: the fed's own Official 4WW Title History thread (promotions/4ww/archive/forum-official-4ww-title-history.html): "Added the two recent title changes. Dark Angel winning the South Wind Championship."

how: His own forum signature bills the reign the longest in the belt's own record, at 85 days.

title: 4ww-east-wind
label: Draven Lox and Dark Angel

won.source: The fed's own Maelstrom II: Eruption: "Your winners, and the inaugural East Wind Champions.... Draven Lox and Dark Angel...."

how: Beat BlackJack and Jaime in the tournament final. Inaugural East Wind Champions.

title: 4ww-east-wind
label: Featured Attraction

won.source: The fed's own Maelstrom III: Legacy, where Featured Attraction defend and retain.

note: Featured Attraction is billed on the 2004 awards ballot as "Jerms & Mike Marvelous".

title: 4ww-east-wind
label: FutureShock

won.source: the fed's own Official 4WW Title History thread (promotions/4ww/archive/forum-official-4ww-title-history.html): "Shoudou & Ukyo Kushinaga won the Mini Tourney at Maelstrom 4 defeating the Devious Brothers to win the Vacated East Wind Titles."

how: Won a mini tournament at Maelstrom 4 for the vacated titles.
note: The belts had been vacated; the fed's own historian recorded the change without a date, and Maelstrom 4's own date is one he asked the board for and did not get.

title: 4ww-west-wind
label: Rustin Slade

won.source: His own roster card: "Former West Wind Champion".

note: Neither end of this reign is dated in the surviving record.

won.source: The fed's own Maelstrom II: Eruption, where he is introduced as the reigning West Wind Champion.

title: 4ww-west-wind
label: Fnord

won.source: The fed's own Maelstrom II: Eruption.

how: Beat Draven Lox after winning the Triple Threat Extreme Iron Man Challenge earlier the same night to earn the shot.
note: Still champion at Maelstrom III in March 2004, where he retains against the Masked Avenger.

title: 4ww-west-wind
label: Kyo Kushinaga

won.source: the fed's own Official 4WW Title History thread (promotions/4ww/archive/forum-official-4ww-title-history.html): "Kyo Kushinaga defeated Tarrant at Maelstrom 4 to become a 2 time West Wind Champ."

how: Beat Tarrant at Maelstrom 4. His second reign; the first is undated in the surviving record.

won.source: the fed's own Official 4WW Title History thread (promotions/4ww/archive/forum-official-4ww-title-history.html): "Bullet defeated Kyo Kushinaga to become West Wind Champ in a Flaming Cross Match on 7/19/04."

title: 4ww-west-wind
label: West

won.source: the fed's own Official 4WW Title History thread (promotions/4ww/archive/forum-official-4ww-title-history.html): "West Wind Title Match / 220 Light Tube, Barbed Wire Rope, 2 out of 3 Falls, 3rd fall is an I quit match / SF- August 10th West defeats Bullet to become WW Champ."

how: Two out of three falls over 220 light tubes and barbed-wire ropes, the third fall an I Quit match.
note: The historian's own note writes the winner as "West"; the 2004 awards ballot's own Upset of the Year category names the same change "Chris West d. Bullet for WWT".

title: 4ww-tempest
label: "Simply Stunning" Sean Summers

won.source: the fed's own Official 4WW Title History thread (promotions/4ww/archive/forum-official-4ww-title-history.html): "the two previous champions before Enigma were Superstar Eddie B and 'Simply Stunning' Sean Summers"; the historian could not find the dates.

note: The fed's own title historian recorded this reign without a date and asked the board for one twice; none was supplied.

won.source: the fed's own Official 4WW Title History thread (promotions/4ww/archive/forum-official-4ww-title-history.html), where Eddie B. adds in his own voice: "Eddie B. defeated Sean Summers! Then he successfully defended it against Summer Andrews and Lee Satima on two seperate dates."
the fed's own Official 4WW Title History thread (promotions/4ww/archive/forum-official-4ww-title-history.html): "Added the two recent title changes... and Enigma winning the Tempest Title."
the fed's own Official 4WW Title History thread (promotions/4ww/archive/forum-official-4ww-title-history.html): "Kris Kanton defeated Enigma on SF to become Tempest Champ."
the fed's own Official 4WW Title History thread (promotions/4ww/archive/forum-official-4ww-title-history.html): "Robb Hardy defeated Kanton to become Tempest Champ on 7/19/04."
the fed's own Official 4WW Title History thread (promotions/4ww/archive/forum-official-4ww-title-history.html): "SF 26th July 2004 - Chris Sanchez defeated Robb Hardy for the Tempest title."

title: 4ww-tempest
label: TJ Anderson

won.source: His own roster card: "Tempest Champion (Current)".

note: His card is the fed's own last word on the belt; nothing after it survives.
